newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Seven Russian police die in blast near Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Seven Russian police die in blast near Chechnya.

text.p: Seven Russian policemen died near Chechnya on Tuesday when the truck they were travelling in was blown up, a regional interior ministry spokesman said.
"They were police brought from various parts of Russia for duties on the Chechen border," the spokesman for the Dagestan interior ministry said by telephone.

He said a bomb had gone off as the truck drove along a road on the outskirts of Khasavyurt, a town in the Dagestan republic bordering Chechnya. "According to preliminary information, seven people died and 13 were injured," he said.
Itar-Tass news agency put the death toll at eight and said 12 were hurt. Interfax news agency said nine police were killed and six taken to hospital.
There have been sporadic armed incidents along the border since the last Russian troops withdrew from Chechnya in January after a 21-month conflict with separatist rebels.
The border troops have accused Chechens of staging armed raids on farms and villages in Dagestan. But the Dagestan interior ministry spokesman said there had previously been no major incidents.
"Things happen on the border but they have been small incidents. There haven't been any big clashes or standoffs," he said.

Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov has accused Moscow of trying to blockade his breakaway region, which says it is already independent despite a peace deal designed to put off the issue of sovereignty for five years.
Relations appear to have been improving with the signing of a memorandum on transporting oil across the region and the two sides have been discussing banking and customs agreements.
